outcome.rationale: Both treatment arms incorporate established active agents (anti-PD-1 backbone) with mechanistically rational additions. Active comparator (BV+Bendamustine+PD-1) builds on proven ADC-chemotherapy-immunotherapy approach. Experimental arm (Chidamide+Decitabine+PD-1) has strong mechanistic rationale (epi-immunotherapy) and case report support, but no phase 2 efficacy data. Primary PFS endpoint at 2 years is feasible but head-to-head superiority uncertain given active comparator. Trial likely to demonstrate activity in both arms (positive for signal-finding phase 2) but may not establish clear superiority. Success depends on prespecified efficacy thresholds and safety profile. Evidence limitations (no direct data, not yet recruiting) prevent definitive prediction.

analysis_trace.content: Phase 2 randomized open-label trial (NCT06563778) comparing Chidamide+Decitabine+Anti-PD-1 versus Brentuximab Vedotin+Bendamustine+Anti-PD-1 in relapsed/refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) patients who are transplant-ineligible or refused transplant, with estimated enrollment of 100 patients. Expected primary completion: 2026-09-01. Status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING. Primary endpoint: PFS at 2 years.

R/R cHL patients post-2L therapy, age 18-75, ECOG <2, at least one measurable lesion >1cm per Lugano 2014. This is a heavily pre-treated population with limited options. Prior autologous transplant allowed if >3 months. Excludes prior exposure to study combinations.

Experimental arm: Chidamide (selective HDAC1/2/3/10 inhibitor) induces tumor apoptosis and enhances immune surveillance; Decitabine (DNMT1 depleter) increases tumor antigen/HLA expression and promotes T cell infiltration; combined with anti-PD-1 checkpoint blockade. This represents an 'epi-immunotherapy' strategy. Active comparator: Brentuximab vedotin (CD30-directed ADC) + Bendamustine (alkylating agent) + anti-PD-1, building on established ADC-chemotherapy-immunotherapy backbone.

Primary PFS (2-year): Time-to-event endpoint requiring survival follow-up. Secondary CRR and ORR (1-year): Response endpoints per Lugano 2014 assessed by investigators. Secondary safety: Treatment-related AE count/percentage. Estimand not fully specified; appears to be ITT or per-protocol per investigator assessment.

Retrieved evidence via EuropePMC searches (pubmed/openalex unavailable). Key findings: (1) Anti-PD-1 monotherapy in R/R cHL shows ORR 60-70%, CR 15-25% (KEYNOTE-087, CHECKMATE-205 historical context). (2) Brentuximab vedotin + bendamustine has real-world evidence in R/R HL (LYSA study, 2026). (3) Case report: venetoclax+chidamide+decitabine induced remission in R/R cHL (2026), suggesting triple epigenetic-targeted therapy activity. (4) HDAC inhibitors and DNMT inhibitors mechanistically enhance checkpoint inhibitor response by upregulating tumor antigens and reversing immune evasion. (5) EHA 2026 guidelines recognize checkpoint inhibitors as standard for R/R cHL. Evidence role classification: direct_numeric=none (no exact trial results); indirect_direction=anti-PD-1 efficacy in R/R cHL, BV+bendamustine activity; mechanism_background=epi-immunotherapy synergy; rejected_mismatch=pediatric studies, non-HL lymphomas, solid tumors.

No direct phase 2 data for Chidamide+Decitabine+anti-PD-1 triple combination in cHL. No head-to-head comparison data. No published results from this specific trial (expected 2026). Registry record unavailable (403). Treatment-related AE rates for this specific combination unknown.

For experimental arm: Base estimate on anti-PD-1 monotherapy benchmark (ORR ~65%, CR ~20%, median PFS ~10-12 months) with modest upward adjustment for epigenetic priming (+10-15% ORR, +5-10% CR, +2-4 months PFS) given mechanistic rationale but phase 2 uncertainty. For active comparator: BV+anti-PD-1 combinations show ORR 70-80%, CR 30-40%; adding bendamustine may enhance further. PFS estimates extrapolated from 2-year timeframe. Confidence reduced due to absence of direct phase 2 data for experimental combination.

Both arms expected to have substantial treatment-related AEs. Chidamide: hematologic toxicity (thrombocytopenia, neutropenia), GI toxicity. Decitabine: myelosuppression. Anti-PD-1: immune-related AEs (thyroid, hepatic, pulmonary). BV: peripheral neuropathy, cytopenias. Bendamustine: myelosuppression, infections. Combination toxicity additive/synergistic; Grade ≥3 AE rate expected 60-80%. No numeric prediction feasible due to lack of specific safety data for these exact combinations.

(1) Experimental arm may not demonstrate superior PFS vs active comparator given BV's established activity. (2) Triple combination toxicity may limit dose intensity. (3) Transplant-ineligible population has poorer prognosis, potentially diluting efficacy signals. (4) Unknown pharmacokinetic interactions between chidamide, decitabine, and checkpoint inhibitors.

Predictions derived from: (a) anti-PD-1 benchmark efficacy in R/R cHL from literature; (b) BV+bendamustine real-world evidence; (c) case report of related epigenetic combination; (d) mechanistic synergy of HDACi/DNMTi with checkpoint blockade. Directional evidence supports both arms showing activity; head-to-head superiority uncertain. All numeric estimates are predictions, not observed results.

Direct phase 2 efficacy data for Chidamide+Decitabine+anti-PD-1 unavailable. Exact statistical analysis plan (hierarchical testing, alpha allocation) not retrieved. Specific anti-PD-1 agents not specified (physician's choice), introducing variability.
